rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for an aromatic or pungent ingredient used to season food.

example.english: When you cook curry, adding a little spice makes it much more fragrant.
example.traditional: 煮咖喱嗰陣，加少少香料會香好多。
example.jyutping: zyu2 gaa3 lei1 go2 zan6 gaa1 siu2 siu2 hoeng1 liu2 wui5 hoeng1 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this for the quality or sensation of food being spicy, rather than for the seasoning ingredient itself.

example.english: The spice in this soup is too strong for me to drink.
example.traditional: 呢碗湯辣味太重，我飲唔落。
example.jyutping: ni1 wun2 tong1 laat6 mei6 taai3 zung6 ngo5 jam2 m4 lok6

rows.note: Use this when something adds interest, enjoyment, or appeal, as in the spice of life.

example.english: This new way of playing adds spice to the game.
example.traditional: 呢個新玩法令個遊戲多咗趣味。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 san1 waan4 faat3 ling6 go3 jau4 hei3 do1 zo2 ceoi3 mei6

rows.note: Use this for a distinctive flavour or characteristic touch, especially one associated with a place, style, or food.

example.english: This soy sauce gives the dish more spice.
example.traditional: 呢種醬油令呢道菜多咗風味。
example.jyutping: ni1 zung2 zoeng3 jau4 ling6 ni1 dou6 coi3 do1 zo2 fung1 mei6
